scope: Selected resident released Qwen validation is complete for ordinary/managed/controlled token parity at 5, 128, 512, 1,500 and 3,000 prompt positions. Independent full-score prefill and three-cached-decode comparisons at 5 and 3,000 tokens are recorded separately from public token-only parity. The 3,000-token managed and controlled runs pass with a 64 GiB managed-domain allowance; practical automatic smaller-chunk selection at 13 GiB and pre-execution refusal at 8 GiB also pass their recorded expectations. Equivalent ordinary chunking demonstrates the same allocation reduction. These results do not establish a total process-memory ceiling or complete the broader applicable family/path integration.
current_findings: Historical initial five-token admission accepted chunk 5 with an incremental requirement of 46,636,254,120 bytes and observed MLX peak of 3,775,128,768 bytes including retained model allocations. Later allocator-corrected five-token runs admitted 9,701,136,060 incremental bytes, as recorded in intermediate_lengths_after_allocator_corrections. Admission is a conservative bound, not measured usage.

Source precision and physical-contiguity facts are recomputed per operation; a targeted audit found no layout-equality-keyed cache that could reuse narrower facts across representations. Logical layout equality alone never authenticates source representation.

The five-token full-score check passes atol=0.25, rtol=0.02 with all four argmax equal; maximum absolute deviation across steps is 0.1586458683013916. The separate 3,000-token full-score comparison is recorded below. Public managed/controlled parity compares exact token IDs, not full scores.

At 3,000 tokens, ordinary full-prefill versus chunk128 MLX peaks are 22,433,750,408 versus 4,813,825,208 bytes (78.542% reduction). Whole-process peak footprints are 24,530,717,936 versus 8,580,140,224 bytes. Both produce [561,6511,314,9338], matching independent reference argmax; chunk128 full scores pass combined atol=.25/rtol=.02 (maximum absolute deviation .275862).

Managed and controlled 3,000-token runs with 128-position chunks both produce [561,6511,314,9338], matching the ordinary reference. Their recorded MLX peaks are 4,811,351,232 and 4,807,681,216 bytes; process measurements and conservative admitted maxima are retained separately.

Practical admission is validated: the 13 GiB request selects 102 positions instead of requested 128 and matches ordinary output; the 8 GiB request refuses before accepted work/output with 11,957,904,935 required bytes versus 6,346,124,670 available managed bytes.

The later graph-construction class-index managed run preserves 3,000-token exact-ID parity and records a 4,820,952,256-byte MLX peak. Its changed native accounting and artifact are retained in graph_construction_class_index; controlled execution was not remeasured on that artifact.
